slots.brief: YDSE diagram with labelled slit separation and screen distance; locate a point with given path difference and ask the fringe order/position at that point.
Energy-level diagram of hydrogen with a few marked transitions; identify which jump emits a given spectral series photon and compute its wavelength.
Force given as a function of position along a straight line; find work done in moving from one coordinate to another by integration.
A solid floats with given fractions of volume immersed in two immiscible liquids layered in a beaker; find the density of the solid.
Cylindrical/spherical charge distribution with charge density varying linearly with radius shown in figure; use Gauss's law to find field at a point inside the distribution.
Ask how the speed of sound in an ideal gas changes when pressure is doubled at constant temperature / when temperature is raised; pick the correct qualitative option.
A cyclic process on a P–V diagram; compute net work done in the cycle by comparing areas of expansion and compression strokes.
A charged particle enters a magnetic field at some angle; identify the direction of magnetic force and whether the speed changes, using right-hand rule.
A string fixed at both ends vibrating in a given harmonic; ask how the frequency changes when tension and vibrating length are both altered by given factors.
A person standing on a lift accelerating upward/downward; ask the apparent weight as a multiple of true weight using N = m(g ± a).
Two projectiles fired with complementary angles with same speed; compare their ranges, maximum heights and times of flight qualitatively.
For a planet, given escape speed, ask for the orbital speed of a satellite close to its surface (or vice versa) using the fixed ratio between them.
A mass on a spring in SHM; ask at what displacement the kinetic energy equals the potential energy (each half of total energy).
Statement-based MCQ: what happens to capacitance, charge and field when a dielectric slab is inserted in an isolated vs battery-connected capacitor.
A loop moved into or out of a uniform magnetic field region in a given time; compute average induced emf from rate of change of flux.
Show field-line patterns around a bar of material in a uniform field; identify which diagram represents a paramagnet/diamagnet/ferromagnet and give reasoning.
Given the expression for electric/gravitational field at a distance, check its dimensional consistency and deduce the correct option by dimensional analysis.
A lens of known glass placed in a liquid of given refractive index; find the new focal length or determine whether it acts as a converging or diverging lens.
A ball strikes a smooth surface obliquely and rebounds; use momentum components along and normal to the wall with a given coefficient of restitution to find rebound speed and angle.
A telescope with objective and eyepiece of given focal lengths separated by a fixed distance; compute magnifying power and ask the condition for final image at infinity.
Use shell theorem: field and potential inside a uniform spherical shell, and how they change if a point mass is placed anywhere inside.
Series LCR circuit with given component values and source frequency; compute the phase angle between current and voltage and state whether the circuit is inductive or capacitive.
Compare rms speeds of two gases at possibly different temperatures; find the ratio using v_rms ∝ √(T/M) with mole data given.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: Photoemission from a metal: statements about threshold frequency, stopping potential and current — identify which quantity depends on intensity vs frequency.
Diagram of a wheel rolling without slipping; relate speed of a marked point on the rim to translational speed, or find acceleration of the contact point.
A car negotiates a banked curve with friction; find the range of safe speeds or maximum speed using tanθ-based formula.
A parallel-plate capacitor with a dielectric slab partially inserted (or two dielectrics stacked); treat as series/parallel combination and find equivalent capacitance and stored energy.
A wire stretched by known amount with a hanging mass; use Y = stress/strain to find elongation or the maximum load for a given breaking stress.
Two long parallel wires carrying given currents; find magnetic field (magnitude and direction) at a point on a line between or outside them.
A particle moving in a straight line at constant velocity; find angular momentum about a point off its path and show/verify whether it stays constant.
A nucleus undergoes alpha decay; compute energy released using given binding energies of parent, daughter and alpha, then find kinetic energy of the alpha particle.

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: Electron accelerated through a potential difference; find how its de Broglie wavelength changes when the accelerating voltage is changed by a factor.
Unpolarized light reflected off a glass surface; use Brewster's law to identify the angle at which reflected light becomes polarized, given refractive index.
A thermometer reads a temperature on one scale; convert it to another scale and pick the correct numerical value.
A Wheatstone bridge with one unknown resistance; use the balanced-bridge condition to find that resistance from the other three arms.
Circuit diagram of two-input gates (NAND/NOR/...) combined; determine the Boolean output for given inputs and name the equivalent gate.
Circuit of a cell with a resistor across which a voltmeter of given resistance is connected; find the voltmeter reading and the error caused by its finite resistance.
For an EM wave in vacuum, compare electric and magnetic energy densities and relate peak field values using E = cB; pick the correct statement.
Average speed question: a body covers two equal distances at speeds v1 and v2; compare its average speed with the arithmetic mean of the speeds.
Circuit with ideal diodes in series/parallel with resistors; determine which diodes conduct and compute the current through a specified branch.
Identify which carbonyl compound gives a positive Tollens' test but negative iodoform/Fehling distinction among simple options.
Among given species, identify the one with a different hybridisation/geometry than the rest (odd-one-out by shape).
For a gas-phase reaction with given Δn, state whether ΔH is greater than, less than or equal to ΔU and why.
Match commonly used antiseptic chemicals (dettol, bithionol, iodine tincture) with their use.
Given initial and remaining concentration of a first-order reaction, count half-lives to find total time.
Ask which noble-gas fluoride does not exist / correct compositions of XeF2, XeF4, XeF6.
Given rate constant of a zero-order reaction, find concentration remaining after a stated time (or time to reach zero).
Use bond enthalpies of reactants and products to compute ΔH of a combustion/formation reaction via Hess-type addition.
Write the correct Ksp expression (with powers) for a sparingly soluble salt; test also solubility in common-ion solution.
From percentage composition of C, H and O, determine empirical formula and then molecular formula from molar mass.
Provide an aromatic ring with substituent(s) in a figure; ask major product of EAS directing the incoming group to correct position.
Match haloalkane substrates with correct elimination/substitution product or reagent behaviour (e.g. Saytzeff vs Hofmann product).
Phenol + CHCl3/NaOH followed by hydrolysis: identify the product and the reaction name (Reimer–Tiemann).
For a given complex ion (octahedral), use CF splitting to decide high/low spin and count unpaired electrons.
Assign R/S configuration to a molecule drawn as a Fischer projection.
Match functional-group detection (Lassaigne's test: N, S, halogen) with correct observation/chemistry.
Evaluate two statements on ionisation enthalpy trends across a period and down a group; pick the correct combination.
Order given alkyl halides by SN2 reactivity / leaving group ability and identify correct sequence.
Ask which of several triatomic/polyatomic species is non-polar despite polar bonds due to symmetric geometry (dipole moment zero).
Give the IUPAC name of a complex (e.g. [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2) or formula from name.
Give electronic configuration of a transition metal ion (e.g. Cr2+, Mn2+) and its oxidation state/d-orbital occupancy.
Propose a two-step conversion of an alcohol/alkene to an ether via Williamson synthesis with correct alkyl halide choice.
Show a substrate structure in a figure; ask which reagent (Lucas reagent sequence) distinguishes the given alcohols by rate/appearance.
Ask why transition metal ions are coloured (d–d transition) and match a given ion with its colour.
Given a set of quantum numbers (n, l, m, s), decide whether it is allowed for an electron; identify the invalid one.
Given E° values of M(n+1)+/Mn+ couples, arrange metals in order of reducing strength.
Arrange given carbanions/radicals by stability with a stated reason (resonance, inductive effects).

slots.archetype: volume from density then PV = nRT
slots.brief: From gas density at given T and P, compute molar mass or volume via the ideal gas equation.
Compute electrode potential of a cell/concentration cell using the Nernst equation with given concentrations.
Evaluate statements on aliphatic vs aromatic amine basicity in gas/aqueous phases and pick correct ones.
Given K for a reaction, find K for the reversed reaction and/or reaction multiplied by 2 (manipulating K).
Ask which indicator/apparatus is correct for a strong acid–strong base titration and why the burette is rinsed with the titrant first.
Show an alkene structure in a figure; give the ozonolysis product(s) and ask which alkene would produce them.
Ask which pollutant(s) cause ozone depletion and which cause acid rain / photochemical smog (identify by chemical reaction).
Arrange given Group 16 hydrides by boiling point / thermal stability or Group 13 oxides by acidity, testing anomalous trends.
Two statements on disaccharide glycosidic linkage / reducing behaviour (e.g. sucrose vs maltose); pick correct option.
Ask which of given substances acts as a protective colloid (lyophilic protecting lyophobic) — e.g. gelatin.
Use r ∝ n²/Z relation for Bohr orbits: compare radius in H vs He+ or Li2+ for the same orbit.
Identify reagents to convert aniline to a target (e.g. benzene via diazonium, or iodobenzene) in correct order.
Given molality and observed vs theoretical freezing point depression, compute van 't Hoff factor and infer association/dissociation.
Sentence with a compound subject joined by 'as well as' or a collective noun where the verb is misused; student must spot the agreement error in one part.
Give a common idiom (e.g. 'to let the cat out of the bag') used in a short sentence; ask for its meaning among four options.
Sentence where the preposition is followed by an infinitive/base verb instead of the gerund; student spots that part.
Straightforward NCERT-level word (e.g. 'candid', 'arduous'); ask for the closest synonym among four simple options.
Single-blank sentence on a familiar context (e.g. weather or daily life) where one moderate word fits best among four choices.
Sentence using a wrong verb-preposition pair (e.g. 'comprises of', 'married with'); pick the option that correctly improves it.
Five short jumbled sentences on a general topic (e.g. a historical monument); four options give possible opening sentences, student picks the correct first sentence.
Four spellings of a commonly misspelled word (e.g. 'accommodate', 'occurrence'); pick the correctly spelt one.
Sentence mixing past narrative with an incorrectly shifted tense in one part; include 'no error' as a valid option, but make one clause tense-inconsistent so it is the answer.
Give a moderately difficult word (e.g. 'frugal', 'lucid') and ask for its opposite among four plausible options.
Blank in a sentence filled by a common phrasal verb (e.g. 'put off', 'call on', 'look into') with the correct particle choice among four options.
Analogy pair such as 'Ship : Captain :: ?' or noun-colon-noun based on relationship (leader/institution); pick the matching pair.
Five jumbled sentences where the first and last are given as fixed; student must order the three middle sentences correctly from four options, on a topic like a scientific process or daily habit.
Give four number pairs (or letter pairs) sharing a common relation (e.g., square, positional difference); one pair breaks that relation — identify the odd pair.
Short family statement about a couple with sons/daughters and grandchildren; ask how many total members or how many males — must deduce gender from given clues.
Give four similar-looking words; ask which one appears first (or arrange in dictionary order) — careful with third/fourth letter tie-breakers.
Two statements with a gap in the middle term; test which conclusion definitely follows and which is only a possibility — select correct option combination.
Mixed alpha-numeric series where each term has a letter block and a number block following separate rules; find the next (or missing) term.
Letter pair analogy based on positional values (e.g., opposite letters or constant positional difference); apply the same rule to find the missing pair.

A word is coded digit-by-digit using a hidden rule (e.g., number of letters between the letter and its alphabet-mirror, or position-based formula); apply the deduced rule to a new word of same length — hard, multi-step deduction required.
Use the definition of a parabola (distance to focus = distance to directrix) to identify the focus of a given parabola.
In a binomial expansion, find r so that two consecutive binomial coefficients are equal (n even/odd cases).
Given a small discrete data set, compute variance by the direct formula and identify it among options.
For a cubic, find the point of inflexion by setting f''(x) = 0 and check sign change.

slots.subtopic: Range of a sin + b cos
slots.brief: Find the maximum and minimum of a cos θ + b sin θ and hence solve a given equation has no solution / find range.
Solve a simple trigonometric equation of the form sin θ = given value and write the general solution.
Solve a variable separable DE of the form dy/dx = f(x)g(y) and apply an initial condition to find the constant.
Count the number of relations / subsets possible from a set with n elements (total, symmetric, etc.).
Integrate an e^f(x)[f(x) + f'(x)] type integrand directly.
Given two groups with known means and variances, find the combined mean and combined variance using pooled formulas.
Evaluate a sum like tan⁻¹x + tan⁻¹y by converting to an addition formula, checking the principal value branch.
Evaluate a first-principles limit for a composite function or a simple chain-rule derivative at a point.
Use Euler-type substitution t = x + √(x² + k) to rationalise and integrate an expression with √(x² + k).
Set up and compute the area between a parabola and a line/second parabola using intersection points as limits.
Solve a linear first-order DE dy/dx + P(x)y = Q(x) using the integrating factor, with an initial condition.

slots.subtopic: Image of a point in a line
slots.brief: Find the image (reflection) of a given point in a given line using the perpendicular-foot method or formula.
Simplify a trigonometric integrand using identities (e.g. half-angle) and then integrate.
Examine differentiability of a piecewise function at the junction point by comparing one-sided derivatives.
Count 4-digit numbers with a digit constraint (e.g. exactly one repeated digit or divisibility by 5) by cases.
Expand and evaluate a scalar triple product to test coplanarity or compute volume of a parallelepiped.
Given a compound statement involving ∧, ∨, negations, select the logically equivalent simplified form.
Given a relation like z + 1/z or |z − a| = |z − b|, find the locus (circle/line) it describes.
From a 2×2 probability table, compute a conditional probability and check independence of two events.
Find the equation of a line through a given point making a specified angle/slope relation with a given line.
Evaluate a limit of a telescoping product or a rational function after factorisation and cancellation.
For a matrix A satisfying a simple relation, compute Aⁿ or a linear combination of powers using the given relation.
Find the locus/equation of a line satisfying two distance conditions (e.g. equidistant points, fixed distance from origin).
Count skew-symmetric matrices of a given order with entries from a set, or find trace properties of such matrices.
State/use basic ellipse or circle properties (e.g. eccentricity, foci of a standard conic) via direct recall.
For two positive numbers with given AM and GM, verify/find related AP–GP properties (e.g. recover the numbers).
Test which of several statements about independence/mutual exclusivity of events is true for described dice/card experiments.
Find the domain of a function with a rational/square-root expression using a sign chart.
Form a quadratic equation whose roots are a symmetric function (e.g. α²+β² or 1/α + 1/β) of a given equation's roots.
Find the value(s) of a parameter making two vectors collinear, then use it for a dot/cross product computation.
Evaluate a small power of a complex number given in a + ib form by direct multiplication.
Determine whether a given function is odd/even and whether it is strictly monotonic on a stated interval.
Count selections of at least one object from distinct types using complementary counting (2ⁿ − 1 style).
Given direction cosines/ratios of a line, use l²+m²+n²=1 to find an unknown component or the angle with an axis.
Identify the conic defined as the locus of a point whose distance to a focus equals its distance to a fixed line (directrix definition recall).
Find the value of a parameter making a 3-variable linear system consistent with infinitely many solutions (determinant conditions).
Find the foot of the perpendicular from a point to a plane/line and then the perpendicular distance.
Find the local maxima/minima of a function by critical-point analysis with a sign chart of f'(x).
Count elements in exactly one of two/three overlapping sets using a Venn-diagram style inclusion-exclusion computation.
Use King's property ∫₀ᵃ f(x)dx = ∫₀ᵃ f(a−x)dx to evaluate an integral by adding the two forms.
